items.line: Elon Musk posts a quoted post with the words "This is not AI" and a laughing emoji. The post it quotes is not in the record here, so what the clip shows is not checked here.
Elon Musk jokes about "Singularity dot Com", a dating site for digital superintelligences.

Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky says that since last night Russia has launched more than 400 attack drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic, spread across many cities and regions. Not checked here.
DiscussingFilm says GTA 6 earned $3.79 billion in its first day and calls it the biggest entertainment launch of all time. IGN carries the same figure and credits Rockstar Games. Not checked here.
Dexerto says a Discord user built an AI "girlfriend" bot you can talk to in a voice call, and that it giggles before answering in the demo. It says viewers are asking when they can try it.

Eric Daugherty says the Nasdaq plunged and wiped out its 2026 gains, and quotes President Trump saying "We've lost $4 TRILLION since the election." Neither the market move nor the figure is checked here.
SpaceX says its Dragon capsule has separated from the International Space Station and is firing four departure burns. It says splashdown is about 29 hours away, off the coast of California.
Stray Kids announce that the "Christmas EveL" music video has reached 200 million views. The post is in Korean and English.
DiscussingFilm shares a first look at a Star Wars and Marvel crossover comic in which Spider-Man meets Luke Skywalker, with the line "I'm Peter Parker, I'm here to rescue you."
Variety reports, citing sources, that the film "Michael" will not be submitted for the 2027 BAFTA Film Awards. The sources did not say why. Not checked here.
ABC News reports life-threatening flooding on both U.S. coasts. It says days of rain have left some Florida neighborhoods under water and another powerful storm is aimed at the West.
Unusual Whales says Bloomberg reports that CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler. Not checked here.
Polymarket says a Neuralink patient plays GTA VI with a chip implanted in the brain, controlling the game with their thoughts. Not checked here.
Marc Lou says his $100K Hackathon disqualified its number one product. He says the work started before November 16 and was a reworked existing product, which breaks the rules.
Fox News shares Christian artist Phil Wickham at its All-American Christmas Tree Lighting, saying "the best news you could ever hear is that God loves you."
Formula 1 posts a clip from the Las Vegas Grand Prix session with Max and Franco going wheel to wheel early on.
KoWatermelon posts that IVE won Best Female Group at the 2026 MAMA Awards, with the line "They are Queen".
PopBase says New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani tore his Achilles tendon playing soccer on Thursday night. It says he will wear a boot for 6 to 8 weeks. Not checked here.

Peter Wildeford posts a clip of President Trump saying he and President Xi agreed to "do some joint guardrails" on AI. Trump says AI is "not artificial, it's super" and may be "too super". The clip is not checked here.
The NFL says the Indianapolis Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones.
MLB says the Dodgers reportedly acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Twins, citing multiple reports including MLB Network's Jon Heyman. Not checked here.

Cebu Daily News reports on a Philippine House bill to create a "Pax Silica" semiconductor, AI and critical minerals zone in Tarlac. It says advocacy groups warn about tax incentives for foreign firms and land leases that could displace farmers and Indigenous people.
Brian Greene shares a video summary of reports that AI may have solved the Riemann Hypothesis. Not checked here.
The Free Press says journalist Matt Taibbi is joining it as a reporter at large for the presidential campaign.
The NYCMayor account posts a 91-second video with the words "We're closing Rikers once and for all." The post does not say how or when.
Aaron Rupar posts a short video of President Trump talking about Democratic majorities. Rupar quotes him as saying "We could end up with great healthcare in our country." Not checked here.
CultureCrave says "Grand Theft Auto 6" has been review-bombed by users on Metacritic and shows a 4.9 rating. Not checked here.
A user posts a joke that a very hot shower is bad for skin and hair, but "being boiled alive" is good for their mental health.
Coin Bureau says Asia's stock markets lost over $1.1 trillion today, with 12 of 13 major indexes down. It lists Taiwan down 6.23% and Japan down 5.06%. Not checked here.
Barack Obama posts a video about trust in institutions. He says this year's Democracy Forum, December 9 to 11 in Chicago, will focus on trust.
The Rapid Response 47 account posts President Trump on Iran. It quotes him saying Iran wants a deal "that's acceptable to me" and that he wants "a real deal, not a fake deal."

Rahul Gandhi posts in Hindi. He says that Modi's complaint that industrialists did not raise pay or create jobs after tax cuts is a confession, and accuses Modi's policies of harming small businesses.

Ed Krassenstein posts a 28-second clip of President Trump with Stephen Miller at the White House podium. He says Trump seemingly endorsed Miller for president over JD Vance and Marco Rubio. Polymarket describes the same exchange as Trump asking Miller if he would like to run in 2028. Not checked here.

Dexerto says the Denver Broncos are bringing Umamusume horse girls to the NFL. It says Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen will appear at the team's December 6 game against the Miami Dolphins. Not checked here.

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi posts a quip that Iran did not know the Israeli ambassador to Washington was the commander-in-chief of the U.S. military. The post he quotes is not in the record here, so what prompted it is not checked here.
Watcher Guru says the FBI was hacked again in a cyberattack on its nationwide crime database, citing CNN. Not checked here.
Nature Unedited posts a video of a whale and says the discomfort the whale had endured for years disappeared in 30 seconds. What the video shows is not checked here.
Watcher Guru says crypto keeps falling: Bitcoin under $56,000, Ether under $1,550, and $650,000,000 in leveraged positions liquidated in the past hour. Not checked here.
Polymarket says a new pancreatic cancer drug, daraxonrasib, halted tumor growth in 90% of patients in an early trial. The post names no source. Not checked here.
TMZ says Macaulay Culkin is returning as Kevin McCallister in a "Home Alone" sequel. Not checked here.
The NBA says James Harden scored 51 points, the most he has scored as a Cavalier, as Cleveland moved to 2-1 in Emirates NBA Cup group play.

Fabrizio Romano quotes Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada, speaking to Sky Sports, on new coach Mauricio Pochettino. Berrada says he has experience, passion and energy and is as ambitious as the club about winning titles.
Adam Schefter shares an ESPN story saying Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud stayed in the "groove" with another three-touchdown night in the Texans' blowout of the Colts.

Gunther Eagleman posts a clip of President Trump ending a press conference. The post says Trump told a reporter who shouted over him, "You really are a rude person. I'm not talking to you," and that they belonged in the back row. The clip is not checked here.

Mario Nawfal posts that a new report says the U.S. is critically short of Patriot and THAAD interceptors, Standard Missiles and Tomahawks. It quotes retired Lt. Col. Anthony Aguilar saying "Firing missiles is not a strategy to win." The post does not name the report. Not checked here.
